directives.title: Monitor £4.5M of current suppliers with Companies House red flags
directives.evidence: 9 current suppliers have Companies House compliance issues (historical payments were made before breaches started)
directives.notes: Historical payments pre-breach — but demand watchlist + proactive monitoring.

directives.title: Scrutinise £2108.6M medium-confidence duplicate payments
directives.notes: Sample audit of top 50 groups by value — different references may be legitimate.

directives.title: Challenge £423.1M suspected split payments
directives.evidence: 1545 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
directives.notes: Classic indicator of bypassed procurement controls. FOI procurement authorisation records.

directives.title: FOI: round-number payments over £5K (£343.5M)
directives.evidence: 1906 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts
directives.notes: Round figures can indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts. FOI invoice breakdown for top 20.

directives.title: Question 2.7x March year-end spending spike
directives.evidence: Northamptonshire Children's Trust spent 2.7x their monthly average in March (£40.0M above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
directives.notes: Request written explanation from s151 officer. Compare with peer pattern.

directives.title: Review 15 rapid-payment suppliers (<14-day cadence)
directives.evidence: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Redacted Personal Data (2.3 day avg, 52478 payments, £111.1M)
directives.notes: Suggests framework contract lacking consolidation OR pass-through arrangement. Request contract register for top 5.

directives.title: Review Benford's Law first-digit distribution (4.8% dev)
directives.evidence: Digit distribution across 370,713 transactions shows χ²=9420.32 (statistically significant due to large sample size), but max digit deviation is only 4.8% — within the normal range for UK council spending patterns. No practical evidence of fabricated invoices.
directives.notes: Statistical noise on large samples; compare with other councils before escalating.

directives.title: Investigate Benford's 2nd-digit anomaly (χ²=4286.89)
directives.evidence: Second-digit distribution across 370,713 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 2.81% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
directives.notes: Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for round-number bias and fabricated invoices.

directives.title: Scrutinise 13 weak-competition contracts
directives.evidence: 13 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: WNC Nightly Purchased Temporary Accommodation DPS  (£3.0M)
directives.notes: FOI tender evaluation reports. Question at Scrutiny why restricted tender was used.

directives.title: Request internal audit action plan on all 9 DOGE findings
directives.notes: Formal letter to Chief Internal Auditor requesting a written action plan covering all DOGE findings. Request named owners, committed timescales, and reporting back to Audit Committee.
